correctness.rationale: The generalized-quadrangle incidence matrix B has BB^T=(q+1)I+A with collinearity eigenvalues q(q+1),q-1,-(q+1) and respective dimensions 1,f=q(q+1)^2/2,g=q(q²+1)/2; singular values of B are q+1,sqrt(2q),0. On the zero-sum subspace of the full 2v powered-distance matrix the exhaustive sectors are balanced-constant F_q(p), paired R±(p) of multiplicity f, and S(p) of multiplicity 2g, totaling 2v-1. R±<0 for 0<=p<=p0=log2(1+1/q), S<0 for p<p0, while F_q(0)=-1 and F_q(p0)>0, with derivative positive for p>=0; hence exactly one F root strictly before p0. Above it F>0 until p0 and S>0 past p0. Endpoint nullspace exactly one-dimensional, so centered Schoenberg Gram rank drops from 2v-1 to 2v-2. Expanding F_q’(0)=q³log(4/3)-q²log(3/2)+qlog2 and Taylor gives the stated q^-3 and q^-4 terms along existing orders. Independent W(2) incidence graph construction and full 30x30 powered-distance eigenvalue comparisons at p=0.1, 0.345784723476,0.6 verified all predicted spectral sectors; finite q never substitutes for general incidence proof.
residual_risks: Independent finite spectral test carried out only for W(2); original package also provides code for W(3),W(5), but those larger numerical runs were not independently repeated here.
